paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: : Loss steps
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the progression of loss values against the number of iterations. The x-axis is labeled "#Iteration" and spans from 0 to 140000, with a linear scale and tick labels appearing every 20000 iterations. The y-axis is labeled "Loss," also using a linear scale, ranging from 2.4 to 3.4, and with tick labels at regular intervals. A purple, solid line labeled "Vanilla" begins at a value of approximately 3.3 at iteration 0 and decreases to approximately 2.6 at iteration 140000. An orange, solid line labeled "StrmLLM" starts at about 3.3 at iteration 0 and declines to approximately 2.6 at iteration 140000. A green, solid line labeled "SepLLM (n=64, H)" commences at roughly 3.3 at iteration 0 and decreases to approximately 2.5 at iteration 140000. A dark green, solid line labeled "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)" initially sits at about 3.3 at iteration 0, and falls to approximately 2.5 at iteration 140000. A light blue, solid line labeled "SepLLM (n=128)" begins at approximately 3.3 at iteration 0 and ends at roughly 2.6 at iteration 140000.
